title: Dean McCormick joins TracPlus to support its European development
summary: The seasoned geospatial and aviation technology specialist will lead TracPlus’s work with civil protection agencies and aerial firefighting operators across Europe.
body_markdown:
Dean McCormick. TracPlus Photo


TracPlus has announced the appointment of Dean McCormick as European account director.


Based in London, McCormick will work with aerial firefighting agencies and operators across Europe. His mission is to bring the technology of TracPlus closer to their operational needs.


His appointment comes as Europe builds its shared aerial firefighting capacity through rescEU and the EU Civil Protection Mechanism, with aircraft from several countries increasingly working together to combat the same fires.


TracPlus already works with Avincis, providing precise operational records and automated reporting for their aerial fleets, across all of their European operations. McCormick’s goal is to bring that same mission visibility, preparedness, and operational insight to the rest of the continent.


Phil Nunn, chief commercial officer at TracPlus, had this to say about the appointment:


“When aircraft from several countries are working the same fire, coordinators need one picture of where they all are, and where they need to be. Dean understands how European agencies operate. He has spent two decades in geospatial and aerospace technology, working closely with governments and international organizations, and his fire risk work at Hexagon gives him first-hand knowledge of the problem we exist to solve. Just as importantly, he shares our belief that technology should fit the mission, not the other way round. Dean’s proximity to European agencies can help ensure we build solutions around their own doctrines, procedures, and chains of command.”


McCormick brings more than 20 years of experience in geospatial technologies, aviation, defence, and digital solutions. He has held positions of responsibility at Leica Geosystems, Hexagon Geospatial, Presagis and Amazon Web Services, focusing particularly in satellite observation, geospatial analysis, and aerospace technologies.


He has worked with major providers such as Airbus Defence & Space and BAE Systems, as well as with governmental and international organizations. At Hexagon Geospatial, he worked on solutions for monitoring vegetation fire risk.


For TracPlus, McCormick’s ambition goes beyond selling a technology platform: It is about offering solutions tailored to European firefighting organizations, understanding both their unique operational needs and their unique constraints.


To achieve this, he works in partnership with industry experts, combining his own experience with institutional insights from the people who best know their systems, their aerial assets, their procedures, and their chains of command.


“Over my career, I have seen what geospatial data can do when it reaches the people making decisions on the ground, and in aerial firefighting, that data can make all the difference. European agencies already have excellent crews and aircraft. What they’re often looking for is a shared, reliable record of the finer details: Positional data, drop sites, capacity. This is especially tricky when several countries are working together on one incident. TracPlus has spent nearly two decades building exactly that. My job is to listen first, understand how each agency works, and make sure that what we offer fits their operation,” said McCormick of his work.


McCormick’s approach rests on one belief: it isn’t for firefighting organizations to adapt to technology, but for technology to meet the requirements of these teams and their critical missions. New technologies need to be an asset out of the box, not an additional consideration.


This combination of international technological expertise and knowledge of the field will help TracPlus support European organizations in strengthening their fleets and identifying areas for development. It will also make it easier for agencies to coordinate information when they deploy together.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by TracPlus.*
